manchoukuo-1942:IMG_5508_1.rationale: The complete 1616–1941 year/event sequence covers successive rulers, wars, diplomacy, railways, government, settlement and industry. manchoukuo-1942:IMG_5455_1.rationale: Each 1912–1944 row equates Christian years with Japanese foundation/era years, Manchoukuo eras and Chinese Republican years. The figures are calendar designations, with no substantive statistical measurements.

japan-1942-43:p1068_6.rationale: The supplied row identifies the French concession at Tientsin, its creation date and an area of about 2,360 se. The concession is the substantive foreign-privilege subject; its measured area makes this a statistical mixed record.

japan-manchoukuo-1934:p2-0003_2.rationale: Five meteorological observatories are identified with latitude, longitude, elevation in metres and establishment year. The inventory concerns facilities supporting scientific observation. There are no atmospheric-condition readings to support weather, and the leased-territory wording does not make colonial governing powers a subject.

japan-1939-40:p1088_1.rationale: Ordinary and extraordinary revenue and expenditure, with totals for the 1936–37 Kwantung budget, organise every numerical row. The leased-territory designation identifies whose accounts these are; no governing relationship or colonial powers are tabulated.

japan-manchoukuo-1940:p0115_6.rationale: The provincial rows count people described by the source as bandits surrendering in 1935, with a total of 6,713. The table reports that category and surrender outcome; it does not identify political aims or military forces involved.

japan-manchoukuo-1938:p1-0965_1.rationale: For ten narcotic stations and annual totals, the columns measure capacity, admissions, persons reported cured, cure ratios and treatment days, separately for opium and other narcotic patients. Treatment outcomes and the substantial opium breakdown support these labels.

japan-1920-21:p0720_3.rationale: The Tokyo electric tramway series gives mileage, daily passengers and daily passenger receipts for 1917–1919. Revenue is an operating measure of the identified urban tram system.

taiwan-tokei-1925:p0263_2.rationale: The complete 66-row 軌道線路及臺車數 inventory lists operators, route lengths, handcars, regional totals and earlier years; the English description explicitly identifies light push-car tracks. Hand-pushed/light railways fit railways rather than the street/interurban service definition of trams.

japan-1939-40:p0696_1.rationale: All expenditure rows fund educational administration, schooling, social education, special education, universities or libraries, with a total in yen. This is a budget devoted to education rather than a general budget with one school row.

korea-tokanfu-1939:p0246_1.rationale: 朝鮮總督府特別會計 records fiscal-year revenue and expenditure, ordinary/extraordinary divisions, indices and surplus, distinguishing 決算 from 豫算. The establishment-date footnote explains the first accounting period; the substantive table is public finance.

japan-1920-21:p0456_1.rationale: The three numbered textual provisions identify food/drink, medicines/compounding methods and harmful articles as not patentable. Numbers enumerate exclusions from patent protection rather than quantities.

japan-1910:p0347_2.rationale: Annual figures count licensed patent medicines and receipts from 1902 through 1906. The licensed medical preparations are the subject; the word patent does not make this an inventions or trademark-registration table.

far-east-1941:IMG_5400_1.rationale: The eight yearly rows measure production of exactly three named commodities: rubber and rice in thousand quintals and tin ore in metric tons. Crop/latex production and ore extraction substantially organise the columns; all three commodity tags represent the complete scope.

japan-1930:p0513_2.rationale: The 1925–1928 series tabulates receipts, payments and their balance specifically for invisible trade in thousands of yen. It does not present merchandise plus capital/current accounts sufficient to classify the whole table as balance of payments.

japan-manchoukuo-1939:p1-0258_2.rationale: Every national/city column is a cost-of-living index for 1929 and 1932–1937; footnotes identify the Japanese compilers and a separate 1914 base for thirteen cities. This is the specific living-cost series rather than a general multi-domain economic barometer.

far-east-1941:IMG_5089_4.rationale: Eighteen golf links/clubs are compared by holes, course length, area where stated and location. These substantial course measurements make the sporting-facility inventory statistical, even though club names and places are textual.

far-east-1941:IMG_5124_2.rationale: The annual rows compare churches, clergy/missionaries and followers for Tenrikyo, Buddhism and Christianity. Both institutions/personnel and adherence are independently measured; cross-religion tags represent the entire table without selecting incidental denominations.

far-east-1941:IMG_4895_1.rationale: Both complete parts count Shinto shrines and priests by shrine grade over five years, with printed totals. Shinto specifically covers these institutions and clergy; no adherent counts support religious-affiliation.

japan-1942-43:p1157_1.rationale: The complete emperor roster (reigns 54–124) pairs monarchs, era names and calendar date ranges. Its Duration of Reign column contains accession/end years rather than measured reign lengths; dates and reign numbers are reference designations.

korea-1942:p0131_1.rationale: The full 24-sport list counts entrants in the 1940 Korea Shrine athletic meet, including combined male/female gymnastics and a total of 20,731. It measures participation, with no competitive outcomes; the shrine name and education chapter do not independently establish religion or education as table subjects.

manchuria-1939:p0091_1.rationale: All 23 self-protective villages are grouped into dated settlement cohorts, with household/member counts and cultivated hectares. These support migration, household demographics and cultivated land. No nationality, sponsoring foreign state or explicit relation to colonial expansion appears in the complete record, so the narrower settler-migration tag and either imperial topic lack sufficient evidence.
review_questions: Can existing supplied documentary context establish that these railway self-protective villages were associated with colonial expansion or foreign state-sponsored settlement? The complete table shows an organised settlement pattern but does not identify nationality or sponsor; migration is retained pending that evidence.

nanyo-tokei-1937:p0041_3.rationale: Both parts count 狩獵免狀 licences by year and branch office, dividing 遊獵, 職獵 and 學術研究其ノ他. This is hunting licensing administration spanning recreation, professional activity and research. The foreign-licence annotations and note that islanders have no applicable entries are incidental, not an Indigenous-peoples subject.

japan-1937:p0409_1.rationale: The two complete parts combine monthly wholesale prices, exports, imports, industrial production, railway freight, bank clearings, note issue and stock quotations. This is a broad economic indicator set; choosing three individual components would misrepresent its scope.

japan-tokei-1938:p0142_1.rationale: All year and locality rows enumerate social-work facilities across coordination/research, child protection, housing and other economic protection, employment relief, poor relief, medical protection and judicial aftercare. The aggregate welfare-institutions tag describes the full multi-function inventory, including the colonial rows, without elevating incidental facility types to separate subjects.

korea-1935-36:p0167_1.rationale: The complete list explicitly identifies urban tramways in Keijo, Fusan and Heijo, plus another Keijo line and others, with kilometres and a total. Confirmed urban tram content supports trams at table level; the less-specific Keijo line and Others do not justify a speculative additional railways tag.
